rich.html:
Bali is a very challenging place to ride a scooter, because of dense traffic, restricted space, bad road quality and hectic crossroads.

Our training is designed for both beginners and those looking to gain more confidence by knowing the ins and outs of navigating on Bali's roads.

Learn essential skills such as safe riding techniques, road etiquette, and how to handle a scooter in busy conditions.

Our experienced instructors ensure that you feel comfortable and are prepared to ride independently. Whether you're commuting or exploring Bali, our training gives you the skills and confidence you need to ride safely and enjoy.

rich.html:
Bali is one of the most challenging environments to ride a scooter because of narrow, winding roads with potholes, intense & chaotic traffic, as well as animals on the road!

We teach you the skills required  to navigate chaotic streets, manage the scooter and get safely from A to B.

Our comprehensive training has been developed by a group of experienced coaches specifically for foreigners (We teach 200 skills / knowledge items).

Trainings are personalized with one, max two participants (if you bring a partner or friend) and teaching adapts to your specific needs, style and learning speed.

Our introductory training (in Ubud or Canggu) is a 2 hour session for which we provide  safety gear and water. We can also organize a scooter, if required.

If you want to learn how to ride (more) safely secure your spot for the next training: (WA: +62-811-3800-4171):

Discover Bali like never before with our guided scooter tours, perfect for those who want to explore the island with a group (or not feel confident enough to ride solo). Our tours are led by local Balinese professionals who take you to stunning, authentic spots across the island. Whether you're a beginner or looking to meet fellow travelers, our tours offer a safe and social way to experience the beauty of Bali. Enjoy riding through lush rice fields, scenic coastlines, or hidden waterfalls while making new friends on this unforgettable adventure. Let us handle the details while you focus on the ride!

Take your Bali experience to the next level - even if you are beginner rider! Slow and steady wins the race

Join us on Nomeo!

• Assist the Injured Safely: Carefully move injured individuals away from traffic, but only if it's safe and doesn't risk further injury.

  • Alert Oncoming Traffic: Have someone signal approaching vehicles to slow down and divert them away from the accident scene.
     

  • Move to Safety: If possible, move vehicles involved in the accident to the side of the road to prevent further collisions.

rich.html:
• Apply Pressure: Use a clean cloth, bandage, or your hand to apply firm pressure directly on the wound.
     

  • Elevate the Injured Area: If possible, raise the injured limb above the level of the heart to slow the bleeding.
     

  • Use a Tourniquet: As a last resort, if the bleeding is severe and not stopping with direct pressure, you can use a tourniquet. Apply it above the wound, between the injury and the heart.

• Clear the Airway: Gently tilt the head back and lift the chin to open the airway. Check for breathing.
     

  • Administer CPR if Necessary: If the person is not breathing, begin CPR. Give chest compressions at a rate of 100-120 per minute and provide rescue breaths if trained to do so.

• Keep the Person Warm: Use blankets, coats, or whatever is available to keep the injured person warm.
     

  • Elevate the Legs: If there are no injuries to the legs, elevate them to improve blood flow to vital organs.
     

  • Stay Calm and Reassure: Talk to the injured person, keep them calm, and reassure them that help is on the way.

Our story: Love Life, Ride Safe

rich.html:
Out initiative for road safety started when we saw people who were new to riding a scooter in Bali get the same type of accidents and painful injuries - which could have been prevented.

Then, early 2024, we were shocked as a fellow traveler in Bali, Marseli from Moldova, died as a result of a scooter crash!

We were sad that we could not help him and vowed to prevent this from ever happening to others!

Life is too precious and beautiful to be severely impacted or ended by a scooter accident!

Thus, we got together and started teaching people coming to Bali how to ride a scooter more safely. Later we offered practical trainings in combination with tours to enjoy Bali - and life in general.

Our initiative helps foreigners to ride more safely and supports the local community, by reducing the number of accidents they may be involved in. We also create connections between locals and foreigners during our tours and support the local economy. Lastly, safer roads support tourism in Bali in general and allow visitors to enjoy their time on the island more.

We wish you safe riding, a happy life and a great time in Bali!
